headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad tool access make Roo Code’s default workspace a dangerous companion to Copilot’s editor-integrated edits.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Roo Code can read/write the VS Code workspace and browser screenshots. If Roo Code places attacker-controlled text into shared files, Copilot may ingest it as trusted context. This is not a guaranteed direct channel, but the shared workspace makes injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Roo Code writes attacker-controlled instructions into workspace files that Copilot later reads
IF Copilot Workspace or chat treats file content as trusted context without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to a read-only branch or copy of the repo
Disable Roo Code edits on files Copilot will consume
Require human review of any file containing model-generated instructions
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-authored content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and Roo Code shares workspace files and can use broad network egress plus MCP. The pair can therefore move sensitive code or secrets from a shared workspace into external model calls. The profiles do not prove automatic exfiltration of secrets, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate repos or clones per agent
Disable MCP servers for Roo Code during Copilot sessions
Limit Copilot context to non-sensitive folders
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before any outbound API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Copilot’s Workspace plans apply edits, and Roo Code runs in the VS Code workspace with filesystem-based sharing. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state; the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files or git branch in the same workspace
IF no external lock or serialized workflow is enforced
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use git worktrees or separate clones
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits for human review, while Roo Code can act with terminal approval and browser/MCP access. If Roo Code consumes Copilot output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into real actions or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the downstream blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Copilot-generated code or instructions without independent verification
IF Roo Code then executes terminal, browser, or MCP actions based on that output
mitigations: Require Roo Code to cite source files before acting
Force human approval on any terminal or browser action
Compare Copilot output against tests before execution
Keep Copilot in suggestion-only mode for critical changes
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and vendor APIs, while Roo Code can send workspace contents to arbitrary configured model APIs and MCP servers. If regulated data is present, the pair can route the same data through different retention and residency regimes. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code is configured with a provider or MCP server whose retention or residency differs from GitHub's
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use only approved providers and MCP servers
Document retention settings for both agents
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data routing
